extracted.intended_audience: comic creators, storytellers, and social-media artists (including users of AI comic tools)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting and designing comic panel layouts to control pacing, reader flow, and emotional impact; includes practical tips and genre-matching for creators using manual or AI-assisted tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide the reader's eye & pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary job of a panel layout is to guide the reader’s eye across the page in the correct sequence (in Western comics: left-to-right, top-to-bottom). The size, shape, and placement of panels do much more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use panel placement to direct reading order; avoid arrangements that confuse flow. Small, uniform panels speed up action or dialogue; a single large 'splash page' slows things down to let readers soak in dramatic reveals. Ensure the layout 'feels invisible'—it should effortlessly guide readers through the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use classic grid structures for clear sequential narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Classic grids (e.g., four-panel, six-panel, nine-panel) are foundational for straightforward, linear storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four-Panel Grid (2x2): balanced and versatile, great for comedic timing and gag strips. Six-Panel Grid (2x3): more room for plot and dialogue without overwhelming the page. Nine-Panel Grid (3x3): excellent for dense scenes or to slow down a moment by breaking it into multiple small actions. Choose grids for tutorials, daily strips, or any sequence that benefits from predictability and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dynamic & asymmetrical panels to create impact and drama
rubrics_metrics.description: Varying panel sizes and shapes creates a visual hierarchy and emphasizes important moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dominant Panel Layout: feature one large panel surrounded by several smaller ones so the large panel captures the main action or emotional beat. Asymmetry draws attention — use it to highlight what matters. Be mindful: overuse can become chaotic; use selectively to punch up key beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagonal and custom grids for energy and advanced storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagonal lines and custom splits create energy, tension, and motion not achievable with static grids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use diagonal layouts for fight scenes, chase sequences, or psychological distress. Diagonals break the static feel of a standard grid and inherently convey motion and urgency. Historically a pro technique, diagonal splits now can be applied quickly with modern tools to get a 'hand-drawn vibe.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Match panel layout to story genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Different genres benefit from different layout families and devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy: simple, symmetrical grids like the four-panel layout to perfect punchlines. Action: asymmetrical and diagonal layouts to convey speed, chaos, and impact. Drama: mix large emotive panels with small intimate close-ups to control emotional pacing. Mystery: inset panels or overlapping frames to highlight clues and build suspense. Education: classic grids for clear, easy-to-follow instructional content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider pacing and reader flow when choosing panel count and size
rubrics_metrics.description: Pacing should determine panel density: more panels usually speed the rhythm; fewer, larger panels slow it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fast pacing: use more panels per page and smaller, evenly sized panels to encourage quick reading. For slow pacing: use fewer, larger panels to give moments weight. Always check that panel arrangement naturally leads the eye without causing confusion; inconsistent flow is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize key moments through panel sizing and shape (visual hierarchy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel size and shape should reflect narrative importance so readers naturally prioritize key beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the most important moments larger, more prominent panels. Consider dedicating an entire page to a single image—a 'splash page'—for pivotal events. Use tall, thin, or wide panels strategically (see vertical/horizontal emphasis) to convey scale or cinematic scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertical and horizontal emphasis for spatial and cinematic effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Tall, thin panels and wide, short panels convey different spatial and cinematic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long, tall panels can convey falling or towering height. Wide, short panels are ideal for cinematic establishing shots or wide group conversations. Choose orientation based on the emotion or spatial idea you want to convey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harness white space and gutters for visual clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The space between panels (gutters) and surrounding white space significantly affect readability and tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard gutters provide clean separation and easy reading. Wide gutters can imply distance in time or space. No gutters (touching panels) create immediacy, chaos, or seamless action. Don't cram the page; proper white space lets panels breathe and prevents visual overwhelm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency vs. strategic variation in series/layout language
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing a default layout creates rhythm for a series; breaking it deliberately has strong impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a consistent default (e.g., a six-panel grid) to build reader expectations. Then break the pattern for dramatic effect—switch to a dynamic or diagonal layout on a critical page to maximize impact. Overusing surprises dilutes their effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use inset and overlapping panels to highlight details or clues
rubrics_metrics.description: Inset panels and overlapping frames are tools for focus and suspense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inset panels can zoom into a critical detail (e.g., a clue in a mystery). Overlapping frames can show concurrent actions or layered perspectives. Use these to direct attention without interrupting the primary flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel border choices (borderless panels, touching panels) affect mood
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel borders — whether present, absent, or touching — alter the emotional and temporal feel of a page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borderless panels give an open, dreamlike feel. Touching panels (no gutters) create immediacy and chaos. Standard bordered panels maintain clarity and traditional rhythm. Pick border style to support the scene’s mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterate and experiment rapidly (especially with AI tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rapid iteration is essential for finding the best layout; AI tools make testing dozens of variants fast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter your script, browse available layouts, generate, review, and then refine. Use iteration to compare rigid grids vs. dynamic ones and to test if a diagonal layout truly adds desired energy. Don't settle on the first result—experiment until the layout serves the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical selection workflow for AI-assisted layout generation
rubrics_metrics.description: A simple, repeatable process helps choose layouts when using a comic generator tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (1) Enter your story/script into the tool; (2) Browse the library of layouts (the guide references 24 distinct layouts); (3) Select & generate with the chosen layout; (4) Review & refine—if unsatisfied, select another layout and regenerate. This workflow emphasizes speed and experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let the story decide — choose layouts that 'serve your story'
rubrics_metrics.description: The best comic panel layout is the one that serves your story and 'feels invisible' to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid choosing layouts just because they look flashy. Prioritize clarity of sequence, correct emotional pacing, and narrative emphasis. The layout should enhance storytelling, not distract from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small, uniform panels as a tool to increase tempo
rubrics_metrics.description: Small, evenly sized panels accelerate the perceived tempo of action or dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use them for quick exchanges, montage sequences, or to create breathless momentum. Conversely, avoid using them for moments that need emotional weight, where larger panels or splash pages are more appropriate.
